profile.reading: This is Aruba S.p.A.s IT2 data center in Arezzo, Tuscany, Italy, operating as the real time duplication partner to the companys sister IT1 facility in the same city. Aruba, founded in 1994 as Technorail S.r.l. before rebranding, is headquartered in Ponte San Pietro near Bergamo and describes itself as the market leader in web hosting and domain registration in Italy, with significant presence in the Czech Republic and Slovakia, alongside cloud services, certified email, digital signature, and general internet services; the company is also a well known sponsor of Ducatis MotoGP and Superbike World Championship racing teams. IT1 Arezzo is built to ANSI/TIA-942-C Rating 4, the former Tier IV standard, and IT2 is connected to it via dedicated high speed multi fiber cabling. Both Arezzo facilities run a 24/7 staffed Network Operation Center with man-down alarm devices for on site personnel safety, are powered by renewable energy certified under the Guarantee of Origin standard, and use Dynamic Free Cooling technology to reduce energy consumption. Aruba has since expanded its Italian data center footprint further with a third campus, the Global Cloud Data Center in Ponte San Pietro, Bergamo, reported at up to 60 megawatts of capacity. Company wide, Aruba reports serving about 16 million users with 2.7 million registered and managed domains, 9.8 million managed email accounts, 9 million certified PEC email accounts under Italian law, and roughly 1 Tbps of internet capacity, operating 7 privately owned and partner data centers across Europe as of its own recent reporting, a network that grew through acquisitions including Actalis in 2009 and Pratiche.it in 2013 and the 2015 launch of its Aruba Business division. Aruba has continued expanding beyond Arezzo and its Bergamo headquarters campus, including a newer data center campus announced for Rome, reflecting the companys broader strategy of building out a geographically distributed, wholly owned data center network across Italy to support its cloud, hosting, and certified email businesses rather than relying solely on third party colocation.
